applicableAreas: Equipment setups in front of four transformer pads
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) depicts four transformer pads (blue rectangles labeled 'Electrical Transformer Pad') at four locations: west of Building 1/2, between Buildings 4 and 5, between Buildings 6 and 7, and west of Building 8. Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows the same equipment locations in context of buildings, parking, driveways, and sidewalks. However, neither sheet shows any delineated setup area in front of the transformers. No dashed lines, dimensions, or text labels indicating a 20-foot × 35-foot setup area (or any alternative dimensions) were found on either the electrical plan or site plan sheets. The transformer locations are shown graphically but the required horizontal space for truck/crane access is not designated.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.3.16 requires a minimum 20 feet × 35 feet horizontal space in front of all AE equipment for crane and bucket truck access. The applicant has not designated or dimensioned this required space on the site plan or electrical plan. While the equipment locations are shown, the absence of a clearly marked and dimensioned setup area means compliance with this clearance requirement cannot be verified. The preliminary design stage does not exempt the applicant from showing how this mandatory clearance will be provided.
findings.comment: No setup areas (minimum 20 feet × 35 feet horizontal) are shown in front of any of the four transformer pads. Design must designate and dimension the required crane/bucket truck access space for each piece of AE equipment per UCM § 1.3.16.

applicableAreas: Vertical clearance space above equipment setups
findings.observation: Sheet 21 shows transformer pad locations but does not indicate any vertical clearance envelope or dimension. Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows building heights ranging from 33'−4.75" to 36'−1". However, no indication is provided of the vertical clearance above each transformer, such as overhead obstructions (canopies, overhanging structures, tree branches, or overhead utility lines). The preliminary electrical design shows no analysis of vertical clearance above the equipment.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.3.16 requires a minimum 35 feet vertical clearance in front of AE equipment for crane/bucket truck access. Without building elevations or vertical clearance analysis, there is no evidence that 35 feet of vertical clearance is (or will be) available at each equipment location. The presence of buildings with 33−36 foot heights in proximity to the transformers raises questions about whether adequate clearance exists, but this cannot be verified without elevations.
findings.comment: No vertical clearance (minimum 35 feet) is shown or verified above any transformer pad. Building elevations are required to demonstrate adequate clearance for crane/bucket truck access, or alternative equipment locations must be provided.

applicableAreas: Transformer pad locations near Buildings 1, 2, 4, 5, 6, 7, and 8; near parking areas and driveways
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows four transformer pads with generic labels only ('Electrical Transformer Pad') and no specifications (kVA ratings, dimensions, or type). Sheet 9 (Site Plan) displays the same transformer locations in spatial context with buildings, driveways, parking spaces, and sidewalks. Vision analysis of Sheet 21 confirmed that no clearance dimensions or lines are dimensioned from any transformer pad to nearby buildings, parking areas, driveways, or sidewalks. The drawing shows relationships graphically but provides zero quantitative clearance verification.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.4 Table 1.10.4 specifies clearance requirements from pad-mounted equipment: minimum 10 feet on hot-stick use area (side with door), 5 feet on sides with operators/controls, and 3 feet on sides without operators/controls (from removable ventilated obstructions). Additionally, buildings affect these clearances—non-brick/masonry buildings trigger the standard clearances; brick/masonry with 2-hour fire rating allows reduced clearances. No building construction types are documented, and no clearance dimensions are shown from the transformers to any adjacent structures. The plans cannot demonstrate compliance with Table 1.10.4 without these dimensions and without knowledge of building construction type.
findings.comment: Clearances from the four transformer pads are not shown or dimensioned on any plan sheets. Design must provide UCM § 1.10.4 compliant clearances (10 ft hot-stick area, 5 ft operator areas, 3 ft other sides) dimensioned from each pad to buildings, parking, driveways, and other obstructions. Building construction type (brick/masonry 2-hour fire-rated vs. non-brick/masonry) must be documented to determine applicable clearance table.

applicableAreas: Access paths to transformer pads and electrical equipment throughout the site
findings.observation: Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows internal driveways, parking areas, and pedestrian circulation. Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows transformer pad and pull box locations. However, neither sheet designates or dimensions a specific truck access path to the on-site electric facilities. No path is labeled with minimum 12 feet horizontal width or 16 feet vertical clearance specifications. While driveways exist on the site, there is no explicit confirmation that they will be maintained to support AE truck access to equipment, nor are the paths dimensioned to verify compliance with minimum width and clearance standards.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.3.16 requires a minimum 12 feet horizontal width and 16 feet vertical clearance for truck access to AE facilities, with surfaces capable of supporting 72,180 lbs total vehicle weight (32,530 lbs maximum rear axle weight). The applicant must explicitly designate, dimension, and label the truck access path(s) on the site plan and verify they meet these standards. Absence of documented access paths means the applicant has not demonstrated compliance with this mandatory requirement.
findings.comment: No truck access path (minimum 12 feet width, 16 feet vertical clearance) is designated or dimensioned on site plan or electrical plan. Design must identify the truck access route(s) to all AE equipment and dimension them to verify compliance with UCM § 1.3.16 standards, including surface load rating specifications.

applicableAreas: Locations of existing utility poles and streetlights adjacent to proposed buildings
findings.observation: Sheet 4 (Existing Conditions Survey) documents existing distribution poles with power lines along Valley View Road (western and southern property boundaries) and shows the overhead utility line (O.H.U.L.) symbols. Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows the site layout and building locations. However, the site plan set contains no building elevation sheets. The README.md lists 39 sheets in the site plan, primarily focused on site plan, grading, drainage, landscape, details, and utility plans—no architectural building elevation sheets are included. Without building elevations, the three-dimensional relationship between existing poles/lines and proposed buildings cannot be verified.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(2) explicitly requires that 'Building elevations shall be provided showing proposed structures with streets, streetlights, and electric poles.' This is a mandatory documentation requirement when electric poles or streetlights exist on or adjacent to the site. The applicant has not provided any building elevation sheets. This deficiency directly prevents verification of clearance compliance between proposed structures and existing overhead electric facilities.
findings.comment: No building elevation sheets are provided. Site has existing overhead electric poles and lines adjacent to Valley View Road. Building elevations are required to show the relationship between proposed structures and existing electric poles/lines, and to verify compliance with clearance standards per UCM § 1.10.3 (7.5 ft horizontal, 15 ft radial clearance from overhead distribution lines).

applicableAreas: Transmission facility locations (if present on or adjacent to site)
findings.observation: Sheet 3 (General Notes) includes Block 20 titled 'Electric Transmission Notes' containing 16 detailed requirements for transmission easements, clearances, and access (e.g., 25-foot clearance zones, 48-hour pre-construction meetings, 46,000 lb tandem axle road support). These notes explicitly reference transmission structures, transmission easements, and transmission wire. However, Sheet 4 (Existing Conditions Survey) does not show visible transmission structures (only standard distribution poles). The preliminary electrical design plan (Sheet 21) does not show transmission infrastructure. Despite the presence of transmission notes, no building elevations are provided that would demonstrate how proposed structures relate to transmission lines.
findings.reasoning: If transmission facilities are present on or adjacent to the site (as suggested by the inclusion of detailed transmission notes on Sheet 3), UCM § 1.16.0(2) requires that building elevations be provided 'showing transmission lines where applicable.' The applicant cannot demonstrate whether this requirement is met or not, because: (1) transmission structures are not clearly documented on the existing conditions survey, and (2) no building elevations are provided in the site plan set. The inclusion of transmission notes without corresponding transmission detail on the existing survey creates ambiguity.
findings.comment: Sheet 3 includes detailed Transmission Notes (16 items), yet transmission structures are not clearly shown on the Existing Conditions Survey (Sheet 4), and no building elevations are provided. If transmission facilities exist, building elevations must be provided showing transmission lines and demonstrating compliance with transmission clearance requirements. If transmission facilities do not exist, the transmission notes should be removed from Sheet 3.

applicableAreas: Relationship of proposed buildings to electric easements and facilities
findings.observation: Sheet 4 (Existing Conditions Survey) identifies 5-foot electric and telephone easements on the north and south property boundaries and a 5-foot public utility easement on the east boundary. Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows the building layout relative to the property boundaries. However, no building elevation sheets are provided that would demonstrate how the proposed buildings relate to these easements or to overhead/underground electric facilities in three dimensions.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(2) requires 'Building elevations showing the relationship between buildings and electric easements/facilities' when electric easements or facilities are near proposed buildings. The site has documented electric easements (5-foot width on multiple boundaries), yet the applicant has not provided building elevations to show this relationship. This is a documentation deficiency that prevents verification of easement impacts and clearance compliance.
findings.comment: No building elevation sheets are provided showing the relationship between proposed buildings and electric easements (north, south, and east boundaries). Building elevations are required to verify that proposed structures do not conflict with easement access or clearance requirements.

applicableAreas: Existing electric poles, overhead lines, and cross arms adjacent to proposed buildings
findings.observation: Sheet 4 (Existing Conditions Survey) shows existing distribution poles with overhead utility lines (O.H.U.L.) along Valley View Road on the western and southern property boundaries. These poles carry cross arms (approximately 8 feet wide per standard distribution pole design) with conductors. Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows building locations in relation to the property boundaries. However, no building elevation sheets are included in the site plan set, which means the poles, lines, and cross arms are not shown on any elevation view relative to the proposed buildings.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(2) explicitly requires that 'Building elevations shall be provided showing electric poles, overhead lines, conductors, cross arms, and property boundaries.' This is a mandatory documentation requirement when overhead electric facilities are present on or adjacent to the site. The applicant has failed to provide this required documentation. Without elevations, the three-dimensional clearance relationship between the existing poles/conductors and proposed buildings cannot be verified.
findings.comment: No building elevation sheets are provided showing existing electric poles, overhead lines, conductors, cross arms, and property boundaries. Building elevations are required to demonstrate adequate clearances from proposed structures to existing overhead electric infrastructure.

applicableAreas: Clearance verification for proposed buildings near existing utility poles with cross arms
findings.observation: Sheet 4 (Existing Conditions Survey) shows existing distribution poles and overhead utility lines. The poles are shown with cross arm symbols (approximately 8 feet wide for standard distribution poles). Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows building locations. However, no section or plan view exhibit is provided that shows the utility poles with cross arms (8 feet width) and dimensions from the outer conductor to the outermost edge of proposed buildings, canopies, or awnings.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.3 requires a 'section and plan view exhibit showing utility poles with cross arms (approximately 8 feet wide) and dimensions from outer conductor to outermost edge of proposed buildings, canopies, or awnings.' This exhibit is a fundamental documentation requirement for verifying compliance with the 7.5-foot horizontal and 15-foot radial clearance requirements from overhead distribution lines. Without this exhibit, clearance compliance cannot be verified.
findings.comment: No section and plan view exhibit is provided showing utility poles with cross arm dimensions and distances to proposed buildings/structures. Design must provide this exhibit with specific dimensions documenting compliance with UCM § 1.10.3 clearance requirements (7.5 ft horizontal, 15 ft radial).

applicableAreas: Clearance verification areas where proposed buildings are near overhead electric facilities
findings.observation: Existing overhead distribution poles and lines are documented on Sheet 4 (Existing Conditions Survey). No clearance exhibits are provided in the site plan set. The preliminary electrical design plan (Sheet 21) shows proposed underground equipment but does not address existing overhead facilities or clearance envelopes.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.3 and UCM § 1.10.2 require that clearance exhibits document AE, NESC (National Electrical Safety Code), and OSHA clearance envelopes. These envelopes define the three-dimensional space that must be maintained clear of obstructions around energized conductors for safety. The applicant has not provided any exhibits showing these clearance envelopes in relation to proposed structures. This is a required exhibit that must accompany the site plan when overhead electric facilities are present.
findings.comment: No clearance exhibits are provided showing AE, NESC, and OSHA clearance envelopes in relation to existing overhead facilities and proposed buildings. Exhibits must be provided documenting the clearance envelopes required by applicable standards (7.5 ft horizontal, 15 ft radial for distribution; larger for transmission).

applicableAreas: Proposed underground electric routing between and near proposed buildings
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows proposed underground electric lines (blue lines) routing from the property boundary to four transformer pads and then daisy-chaining to building meter banks. Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows the building footprints. Vision analysis of Sheet 21 confirmed that 'there are absolutely no dimensions shown on this sheet that quantify the relationship or distance between the proposed electrical facilities and the proposed buildings. The relationships shown are purely graphical.'
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(2) requires that 'an exhibit be provided showing dimensions from proposed buildings to proposed electric routing.' This is a mandatory documentation requirement to verify that proposed underground electric facilities maintain adequate clearances from building foundations (minimum 60 inches per UCM § 1.10.5). Without dimensioned exhibits, the applicant has not demonstrated that the underground routing will comply with clearance standards.
findings.comment: No exhibit is provided with dimensions from proposed buildings to proposed electric routing. Design must provide dimensioned drawings showing the distance from each building footprint to the proposed underground electric conduit and lines, demonstrating compliance with UCM § 1.10.5 (minimum 60 inches from customer buildings).

applicableAreas: All proposed buildings in proximity to AE equipment
findings.observation: Sheet 9 (Site Plan) provides building type information (4-Plex, 5-Plex, 6-Plex), gross floor areas, and unit counts. However, there is no documentation of building construction type (e.g., 'brick or masonry with minimum 2-hour fire rating' vs. 'non-brick or masonry'). No architectural notes or specifications are provided indicating the exterior wall construction materials or fire ratings for any of the eight buildings.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.4 Table 1.10.4 distinguishes between brick/masonry structures with minimum 2-hour fire rating (allowing reduced clearances from equipment) and non-brick/masonry buildings (requiring standard clearances). The clearance requirements from pad-mounted equipment depend on building construction type. Without this information documented on the plans, the applicant cannot demonstrate compliance with the table, and the reviewer cannot determine which clearance standard applies. Per the grouping's regulatory overview, 'Default assumption is non-brick/masonry unless plans explicitly document brick/masonry construction with 2-hour fire rating.'
findings.comment: Building construction types are not documented on plans. Specify the construction type for each building (e.g., 'brick/masonry with 2-hour fire rating' or 'non-brick/masonry') on site plan or architectural notes to enable clearance verification from equipment per UCM § 1.10.4 Table 1.10.4.

applicableAreas: Plat notes and general notes on cover sheet and grading/landscape plans
findings.observation: Sheet 3 (General Notes), Block 20 includes 16 detailed 'Electric Transmission Notes' referencing transmission structures, transmission easements, transmission wire, and access requirements (e.g., 25-foot clearance zones, 48-hour pre-construction meetings, 46,000 lb tandem axle road support, fire hydrants 20+ feet from transmission). Sheet 4 (Existing Conditions Survey) does not show any transmission structures or lattice towers—only standard distribution poles are visible. The Preliminary Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21) does not show any transmission infrastructure. Facts.md confirms the site is outside the 100-year floodplain and within a typical urban context.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(8) requires that transmission notes appear on cover sheets, plat notes, grading plans, and landscape plans ONLY when transmission facilities (60kV+, large structures) are present on the site. Conversely, these notes must be REMOVED if no transmission facilities exist. The applicant has included 16 transmission-specific notes (Block 20 on Sheet 3) but has not clearly documented whether transmission facilities exist. The existing conditions survey does not show transmission structures. If transmission does not exist, the notes should be removed. If transmission does exist, it must be clearly documented on the existing conditions survey and the plans must demonstrate compliance with transmission clearance requirements.
findings.comment: Resolve transmission facility status: Either transmission structures are present on or adjacent to the site (in which case they must be clearly documented on the existing conditions survey and transmission clearance compliance must be demonstrated), or transmission notes in Sheet 3 Block 20 should be removed per UCM § 1.16.0(8) requirements that notes match actual site conditions.

applicableAreas: Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21) and preliminary design coordination
findings.observation: Sheet 21 title block explicitly states 'Preliminary Electrical Design Plan.' The sheet shows transformer locations, pull boxes, underground lines, and meters with minimal specifications. However, there is no explicit note on the electrical plan or general notes stating that the electric facilities are 'conceptual design,' 'not final design,' or similar language. The word 'Preliminary' appears only in the sheet title.
findings.reasoning: When Austin Energy has not completed final electrical design, plans must include explicit disclaimers that facilities are conceptual and not for bidding purposes, and that final design will be coordinated with Austin Energy. While the title 'Preliminary' conveys some design stage information, it is not a sufficient standalone note. The grouping's regulatory overview identifies this as a 'Common Violation Pattern': 'Plans show conceptual electric facilities marked as "final" or "approved". When AE Design has not completed final electric design, plans must include disclaimers that facilities are conceptual and not for bidding purposes, and that final design will be coordinated with Austin Energy.' An explicit text note stating the design is conceptual must be added to make this status clear to all reviewers and construction teams.
findings.comment: Add explicit note to Preliminary Electrical Design Plan stating that electric facilities shown are conceptual design and subject to final coordination with Austin Energy, and that this preliminary design is not approved for construction or bidding purposes.

findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) contains utility notes and disclaimers about the application not constituting verification of all data and engineer responsibility for completeness and accuracy. However, there is no note explicitly stating that 'electric facility layout shown should not be used for bidding purposes.'
findings.reasoning: When electric facilities are shown in preliminary or conceptual design stage, UCM standards and reviewer convention require a note clearly stating the layout should not be used for bidding. This prevents contractors from using incomplete preliminary designs for cost estimation and prevents problems during construction when final designs differ. The absence of this note leaves ambiguity about whether preliminary facilities can be bid on.
findings.comment: Add note to Preliminary Electrical Design Plan stating: 'Electric facility layout shown herein is preliminary design and should not be used for bidding purposes. Final electric design and coordination with Austin Energy is required before construction.'

applicableAreas: Transformer pad locations relative to parking and traffic areas
findings.observation: Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows 88 parking spaces (10 surface, 78 garage) and internal driveways. Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows four transformer pads: one west of Buildings 1/2 adjacent to a driveway curve, one between Buildings 4 and 5 near parking/circulation, one between Buildings 6 and 7 near parking/circulation, and one west of Building 8 near the property line. Vision analysis indicates that transformers appear to be in close proximity to parking and traffic areas, but 'there are absolutely no dimensions shown on this sheet that quantify the relationship or distance between the proposed electrical facilities and the proposed buildings.' Distances from transformers to parking/traffic areas are not dimensioned.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.4 requires that 'Equipment pads be located within 6 feet of parking/traffic areas for AE truck accessibility (unless otherwise specified by AE Design).' This requirement ensures that AE vehicles can position themselves close enough to equipment for safe and efficient maintenance. The applicant must either: (1) demonstrate that equipment pads are within 6 feet of parking/traffic areas (with dimensions), or (2) provide written AE Design approval if different spacing is used. Neither has been provided. The lack of dimensions prevents verification of compliance.
findings.comment: Dimension the distance from each transformer pad to the nearest parking area or traffic lane to verify compliance with UCM § 1.10.4 requirement that pads be within 6 feet of parking/traffic for AE truck accessibility. If distances exceed 6 feet, provide written Austin Energy Design approval for alternative spacing.

applicableAreas: Transformer pad locations near sidewalks and pedestrian paths
findings.observation: Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows concrete sidewalks and decomposed granite walkways throughout the site near the buildings and around the detention pond. Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows transformer pad locations. However, there are no dimension lines or text specifying the clearance distances from any transformer pad to the adjacent sidewalks or pedestrian paths.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.4 requires that 'Equipment pads be located minimum 2 feet from back of sidewalks.' This requirement provides space for sidewalk maintenance and prevents equipment from interfering with pedestrian circulation. Without dimensioned drawings, the applicant has not demonstrated that this minimum 2-foot clearance is maintained at all transformer locations. Visual proximity does not constitute dimensional compliance verification.
findings.comment: Dimension the distance from each transformer pad to the back (furthest from street/building) of adjacent sidewalks to verify minimum 2-foot clearance per UCM § 1.10.4. If any pad is less than 2 feet from sidewalk, redesign pad location.

applicableAreas: Underground electric lines routing to buildings and electrical equipment
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows underground electric lines (depicted as solid blue lines) routing from the property boundary through the center of the site, connecting to the four transformer pads and daisy-chaining to building meter banks (located on building walls). Vision analysis found: 'There are no dimensions shown indicating the clearance or offset distance of the underground electrical routing from the building foundations or other structures.' The underground conduit is shown graphically but without dimensional clearances to buildings.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.5 requires a minimum 60 inches (5 feet) horizontal clearance from AE underground cable, conduit, and underground facilities to customer building foundations and permanent structures (except other utilities, which require 12 inches minimum; gas/fuel/steam require 24-36 inches). Without dimensioned drawings showing the distance of the underground lines from building foundations, the applicant cannot demonstrate compliance with this requirement. This clearance is critical for future excavation safety and building maintenance.
findings.comment: Provide dimensioned underground utility plan showing minimum 60-inch horizontal clearance from proposed underground electric conduit to all building foundations and permanent structures per UCM § 1.10.5. If any location has less than 60 inches, provide alternative routing or written approval from Austin Energy Design.
